title: Agent-driven Jenkins diagnosis, repair and targeted replay
summary: Shared repair-jenkins skill reconstructs actual failed cluster environments, iterates on targeted fixes and returns reviewable patches.

dates.note: Exact start/end dates are not documented. Technical mechanisms are reported in the October 5, 2026 snapshot; any later owner clarifications are cited per fact.

facts.text: Built repair-jenkins, a team-used Codex skill that investigates failed Interconnect Architect GUI Playwright tests in the actual Jenkins cluster checkout, implements fixes and reruns the failing tests.
The repair workflow handles flaky tests, legitimate defects in test code and application/source defects requiring targeted fixes.
The diagnosis/fix/retest loop runs autonomously after invocation, requires three consecutive clean passes and returns changes for human patch review and Git commit/push.
Reconstructed matrix-specific failures from Jenkins metadata, JUnit and cell logs, preserving recorded revisions and LSF execution constraints.
Michael reports substantially reduced debugging effort against a manual alternative taking hours to days; no automated elapsed time or percentage saving was measured.
Used isolated repair worktrees, an alternate Git index for cumulative binary patches, and content/mode/symlink inventories to bind validation to synchronized changes while preserving unrelated work.
The snapshot reports 52 repair test definitions with fixtures from two Jenkins builds; those definitions are not a live pass count.

notes: Frequent personal use and other team users are confirmed; exact team count, patch volume and overall repair success rate are not.
Do not describe automatic commit/push/publication. The hours-to-days manual baseline is a direct owner report, not a timed comparative study.
